🚨 When does aggressive business become a governance issue?
The recent HDFC Bank – MSRDC case is an interesting reminder that strong financial performance alone is not enough. Corporate governance matters just as much.

📌 What happened?

The issue relates to HDFC Bank's arrangements with the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) to attract large deposits in 2017 and 2021.

Media reports alleged that around ₹45 crore was routed through marketing-related payments to secure deposits, raising questions about whether RBI guidelines on deposit pricing were followed.

🔎 The Investigation

Following the allegations:
✅ HDFC Bank's Audit Committee initiated an internal review.
✅ A Special Disciplinary Committee of Independent Directors examined the matter.
✅ Earlier, independent external law firms also reviewed governance concerns raised by the bank's former Chairman and found no evidence supporting broader allegations of misconduct.

👥 Senior executives involved

The Board took disciplinary action against:
• MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan
• CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan
• Group Head – Retail Assets Arvind Vohra

⚖️ What was the conclusion?

The committee concluded that there was no evidence of:
❌ Mala fide intent
❌ Personal enrichment
❌ Improper motive

However, it held that the conduct amounted to "business overreach" and could represent a potential divergence from RBI directions.

💰 Penalty imposed

The Board:
• Issued formal warning letters.
• Imposed a ₹1 lakh penalty on each of the three senior executives.
• Decided to inform the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) about the outcome.

🔮 What happens next?

The case is not necessarily over.

➡️ RBI will review the findings and may decide whether any further regulatory action is required.
➡️ The matter has also delayed the process for the CEO's reappointment while governance reviews continue.

💡 Key takeaway

This case demonstrates an important governance principle:

Not every compliance lapse involves fraud—but even without personal gain, crossing regulatory boundaries can lead to disciplinary action, reputational damage, and increased regulatory scrutiny.

For auditors, finance professionals, and risk managers, this is a reminder that strong internal controls, ethical decision-making, and compliance culture are just as critical as achieving business targets.
